name: Pale Magenta
lede: Pale Magenta is a soft, purplish pink first plated by Robert Ridgway in 1912, long before the word magenta's modern pastel sense took hold.

sections.title: A modifier, plated in 1912
sections.body:
The library's earliest source for Pale Magenta is Ridgway's 1912 color dictionary, plate XII, hue 67, tone b, a scan of an aged plate and so only an approximation; ISCC-NBS 1955 and Wikipedia carry it afterward, and the xkcd 2010 survey recorded the plain descriptive name again [1]. It is built on the modifier grammar *pale* + *magenta*, lightening [[magenta|Magenta]] itself [1]. At hex #D767AD it measures lightness 59 and chroma 55 in LCH [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[pale-magenta|Purplish Pink]], only 3.5 CIEDE2000 units away and read as almost the same color, followed by [[light-rosolane-purple|Light Rosolane Purple]] at 4.0 and [[china-pink|China Pink]] at 4.9 [2]. The library separately logs Mallow Purple, Sky Magenta and Super Pink as near-duplicate names [1]. The nearest gem comparison is raspberry-colored rhodolite [[gem:garnet|garnet]], 7.9 units off, and a close relative turns up in [[film:barbie|Barbie]]'s fluorescent pink sets, 7.5 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a pink this saturated covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That describes a gap in this archive's holdings of Old Master and Impressionist work rather than a claim that no painter ever mixed a pink this bright [4].
